title: Config diff modal: redaction warning, safe preview, and access request UX
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Design how redacted fields are displayed in the Incident Bot v2 config diff experience (Slack card + modal). This includes: (1) clear warnings when redaction occurred, (2) a “safe preview” so responders can still see what changed without exposing sensitive values, and (3) an explicit path to request elevated access (break-glass for Sev0/Sev1) with audit messaging.

Context
- During incidents, responders often need to quickly confirm whether config changes (feature flags, routing policy, quotas, model pins) correlate with symptoms.
- We must prevent tenant/customer data leakage in Slack. Redaction will happen by default; some users may have an elevated scope for unredacted inspection under audit.
- Bot v2 will render a Config diff “card” in the incident thread, with a “View diff” action that opens a Slack modal (pagination for long diffs).

Goals
- Reduce confusion: responders should immediately understand if they’re seeing a partial diff due to redaction.
- Keep the diff actionable: even with redaction, indicate which keys/paths changed and what kind of change occurred (added/removed/modified).
- Make the security posture explicit: show “audited” messaging and a clear request flow for elevated access.
- Avoid adding noise in the #incidents thread: detailed redaction messaging should live primarily in the modal, with a compact hint in the card.

Non-goals
- Do not design a new permissions system; align with existing bot scopes + break-glass policy.
- Do not expose raw values in the safe preview.

Proposed UX
A) Thread card (compact)
1) Card header: “Config diff (customer-safe)”
2) Summary line includes counts:
   - “12 changes • 4 fields redacted”
3) Status chip (right side):
   - Default: “Safe view”
   - If user has elevated scope (detected by backend): “Privileged view (audited)” (only shown when actually viewing privileged content)
4) Primary action: “View diff” (opens modal)
5) Secondary action (only when redaction_count > 0): “Why redacted?” (opens modal anchored to the redaction explainer section)

B) Diff modal (primary surface)
Modal title: “Config diff — Safe view”

B1) Persistent warning banner (only if any redaction occurred)
Banner copy:
- Title: “Some fields are redacted in Slack”
- Body: “Values that may contain secrets or tenant-sensitive data are hidden. This view is safe to share in #incidents.”
- Inline link: “Learn what gets redacted” (opens an in-modal section; no external navigation by default)
- CTA button (conditional): “Request elevated access”

B2) Safe preview rules (what we show in the diff)
We show key paths and change type, but redact values.
- Modified field example:
  - key path visible (if allowlisted): `routing.fallback_policy` (or `flags.streaming_enabled`)
  - old/new values replaced:
    - old: “<redacted>”
    - new: “<redacted>”
  - if field name/path is NOT allowlisted, show:
    - “<redacted field> changed” (no path)

- Added/removed field examples:
  - “Added: flags.new_scheduler_mode = <redacted>”
  - “Removed: quota.per_minute = <redacted>”

- When value is non-sensitive but still redacted due to policy ambiguity, we still redact (conservative) but tag reason as “policy” in the explainer.

B3) Redaction indicators inline
- Redacted values render as a consistent token: “<redacted>” (monospace, subdued)
- Each redacted line has a small “Redacted” pill (grey) on the right; clicking opens a small in-modal popover with:
  - “Reason: secret/tenant-sensitive/policy” (backend-provided category)
  - “This action is audited when viewed unredacted.” (always shown)

B4) “Learn what gets redacted” explainer (in-modal section)
Collapsible section with:
- “We redact:”
  - secrets (API keys, credentials, tokens)
  - tenant/customer identifiers or payload-derived values
  - any field not on the allowlist for Slack rendering
- “We still show:”
  - which config area changed (when allowlisted)
  - whether the field was added/removed/modified
  - timestamps + actor/service that pushed config (if available)
- Link (secondary) to internal doc: “Incident context redaction standard” (Confluence). Keep as a standard hyperlink; does not auto-open.

C) Elevated access request flow
C1) Default users (no privileged scope)
- Show CTA button: “Request elevated access”
- Clicking opens a Slack dialog (simple form) with prefilled context:
  - Incident channel + thread link
  - Incident severity (if available)
  - Service + region
  - Tenant identifier (ONLY if already present in safe context; do not fetch new tenant data)
  - Free-text “Why do you need unredacted values?” (required)
- Submit result:
  - Confirmation: “Request submitted. Security/on-call approval required. This request will be audited.”
  - Also posts a private ephemeral message to the requester with next steps.

C2) On-call break-glass (Sev0/Sev1 only)
- If the incident is tagged Sev0/Sev1 in the thread (or user explicitly selects in the form), show an additional option in the dialog:
  - “Use break-glass (time-limited)”
- Copy:
  - “Break-glass grants temporary privileged access and is logged to audit. Only use when needed to mitigate active Sev0/Sev1 incidents.”
- UX outcome:
  - Provide a single copyable command (exact command TBD by eng):
    - Example placeholder: `/incident-bot breakglass config-diff --ttl=60m --reason="<text>"`
  - Provide an “I understand” checkbox gate before revealing the command (prevents accidental use).

C3) Privileged view (user already has scope)
- Modal title changes: “Config diff — Privileged view (audited)”
- Add a stronger banner:
  - “Privileged content. Viewing is audited and retained.”
- Provide an explicit “Return to safe view” link.

D) Edge cases / degraded mode
- If diff is empty due to permission or fetch failure:
  - Show empty state with clear cause:
    - “Config diff unavailable (timeout)” or “Config diff unavailable (missing scope)”
  - Provide “Open Console” deep link (if available) and “Retry” button.
- If diff is truncated/paginated:
  - Keep the redaction warning banner visible across pages.

Copy / terminology decisions
- Use “Safe view” instead of “Redacted view” to reinforce shareability.
- Use “Privileged view (audited)” instead of “Unredacted” to emphasize logging and seriousness.
- Use “Request elevated access” rather than “Request unredacted,” to avoid implying approval is automatic.

Accessibility
- Banner uses icon + text; do not rely on color alone.
- “<redacted>” token has accessible label: “redacted value.”
- Pills and popovers keyboard navigable.

Design deliverables
- Figma frames:
  - Card variants: no redaction / redaction present / privileged
  - Modal variants: safe with redaction, safe without redaction, privileged with audit banner
  - Dialog: request access + break-glass gated flow
- String table in Figma (exact copy above) for engineering handoff.

Acceptance criteria
- Engineering can implement without additional copy/interaction decisions.
- Redaction is visible within 2 seconds of opening modal (banner at top).
- “Request elevated access” path is explicit and includes audit messaging.
- Safe preview never shows raw values.
